_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). MOSTLY FOLIAGE -- the richest leaf tile in the bottom row after t001. The right two thirds is ONE enormous deciduous tree seen from close range: a thick gnarled ochre trunk rising at x~0.70, heavy limbs radiating left and right, and a canopy of large outlined pointed leaves (夾葉) filled with a blue-green wash that covers everything from x 0.36 to the right edge, top to y~0.80. One great bough reaches LEFT across the tile to x~0.09 at y 0.33-0.63; that bough is the single most animatable shape here. The left third is a different thing and is the trap: pale ochre boulder ledges drawn with wandering contour outlines, VEILED by a second, much finer foliage layer of small 介-shaped leaf clusters hanging on long thin drooping stalks. Those small clusters are real leaves (they carry the same blue-green wash) but they are interleaved with the rock they hang in front of, so the veil boxes below CANNOT be tight -- they are search regions, and a per-pixel green-wash mask is required inside them. Everything ochre without wash is rock or wood. Three specific decoys: (1) the vertical stack of rounded ochre lumps at x 0.34-0.56, y 0.50-0.96 looks at thumbnail size like a second trunk and is a PILE OF BOULDERS -- no bark, no branching, contour outlines only; (2) the pinkish-orange patches at the bottom right are ROCK FACES washed pink and stroked with long parallel 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre lines that fan downward -- at a glance the fan reads as a spray of needles, up close there is not one leaf glyph in them; (3) the long ochre chains of small loops hanging from x 0.14 to 0.46 are woody vines/lianas, bare, and must not move with the leaves. Bottom left is dark ink-wash foreground rock. A robed figure in fine outline with no wash stands clipped by the LEFT EDGE at y 0.41-0.60.

objects.name: crown of the great tree, upper right
objects.note: solid blue-green 夾葉 wall, clipped by the top edge. Densest leaf mass in the tile; the ochre limbs threading through it are wood and should be cut out of the mask by ink-colour, not by shrinking this box

objects.name: canopy band right of the trunk, upper middle
objects.note: continuous with canopy-crown-upper-right; split only so the mask stays off the trunk fork at x~0.68

objects.name: leaf mass sloping down-left off the crown
objects.note: the canopy's left edge slopes down-left through here -- at y 0.22 leaves start at x~0.52, at y 0.44 they start at x~0.30. The box therefore has bare silk in its upper-left corner

objects.name: tip of the great left bough
objects.note: the farthest-left reach of the big tree, hanging over bare silk and the figure. Clean silhouette against an empty ground -- the best hinge subject in the tile

objects.name: body of the great left bough
objects.note: large pointed leaves in overlapping sprays on a thin ochre branch. Below y 0.60 the leaves thin out and rock takes over -- do not extend this box lower

objects.name: leaf mass left of the trunk, middle
objects.note: right edge stops at x 0.67 where the trunk begins; do not push right

objects.name: leaf mass right of the trunk, upper
objects.note: a major ochre limb runs out right through this box at y 0.47-0.56; that limb is wood

objects.name: leaf mass right of the trunk, lower
objects.note: left edge held at 0.76 to stay clear of the trunk, which is x 0.655-0.755 at this height

objects.name: low leaf spray hanging under the trunk fork
objects.note: the lowest blue-green leaves on the big tree. Below y 0.81 everything is rock and root -- the pink hemp-fibre rock face sits directly under this box and must not be swept in

objects.name: small dark-ink leaf cluster beside the trunk
objects.note: pinnate dark-ink fronds with NO blue-green wash, drawn much darker and spikier than the canopy around it -- a different plant growing in front of the rock. Easy to miss because it reads as a dark blot at thumbnail size, and easy to mislabel as rock because it has no colour. It is leaves: the glyphs are repeated, stalked and paired

objects.name: fine hanging leaf veil over the upper-left rock ledges
objects.note: SEARCH REGION, NOT A TIGHT BOX. Small 介-shaped blue-green clusters on long fine drooping stalks, drawn OVER the ochre boulder ledges behind them. Roughly half the pixels in this box are rock. Any mask built from this box must be filtered per-pixel on the blue-green wash; using the box itself as a foliage mask would animate the rock, which is the exact defect that got the earlier pass rejected

objects.name: fine leaf veil on the pale silk between rock and canopy
objects.note: sparser than the veil to its left -- scattered small clusters on near-empty silk. Same per-pixel caveat

objects.name: fine leaf veil down the left edge, middle
objects.note: hangs behind and around the robed figure; the figure's own outline is inside this box and must be excluded

objects.name: fine leaf veil down the left edge, lower
objects.note: thinning out as it meets the dark foreground rock below

objects.name: fine leaf veil over the grey rocks, lower centre
objects.note: the largest patch of the small-cluster layer, drawn straight over grey ink-wash boulders. Highest rock contamination of any box in this file -- treat as a hint, mask on colour

objects.name: gnarled trunk of the great tree
objects.note: thick ochre column with a knot-hole at y~0.66 and vertical bark strokes; runs from the fork down behind the roots at the bottom edge. RIGID -- if this moves the whole tree reads as rubber

objects.name: major limb sweeping left out of the fork
objects.note: the wood carrying canopy-bough-left-main; mostly hidden under leaves, visible in gaps. A hinge should pivot the leaves about this limb, not displace it

objects.name: major limb running right to the tile edge
objects.note: continues into t003

objects.name: bare ochre vines hanging down the centre-left
objects.note: chains of small ochre loops dropping in long vertical strands from the canopy to the rocks -- woody lianas, no leaves on them, no wash. They are NOT part of the leaf veil they hang through, and they are not rock either. Left as motion:none because a swinging rope needs its own treatment; if anyone later wants them to swing, they hinge from the top, not from the canopy

objects.name: ochre boulder ledges, upper left
objects.note: wandering ribbon contours filled with flat ochre-brown, no wash and no leaf glyphs. The fine leaf veil hangs in front of them -- that overlap is why veil-foliage-upper-left cannot be tight. NEVER animate

objects.name: vertical stack of rounded boulders, centre
objects.note: THE MAIN DECOY IN THIS TILE. At thumbnail size this column of stacked ochre lumps reads as a second tree trunk. Up close it is 礬頭-style rounded rock: pure contour outlines, no bark strokes, no branching, no leaves anywhere on it

objects.name: dark ink-wash foreground rocks, bottom left
objects.note: the darkest passage in the tile; broad grey-black wash with dotted texture. NEVER animate

objects.name: grey boulders along the bottom edge
objects.note: clipped by the bottom edge; continues into t006

objects.name: exposed roots over rock, bottom right
objects.note: long parallel 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre strokes fanning downhill; root and stone are drawn with the same stroke here and are not worth separating. Rigid either way

objects.name: pink-washed rock face under the low canopy
objects.note: DECOY. A colour-threshold pass that looks for 'not grey' will grab this: it carries a warm pink-orange wash and its hemp-fibre strokes fan out in a spray that mimics a clump of needles. There is not one leaf glyph in it. This is the family of surface a previous pass animated by mistake

objects.name: second pink-washed rock patch, lower right
objects.note: same decoy as rock-pink-face, smaller, and it sits immediately under dark-leaf-cluster-right -- the two are adjacent and opposite labels, so check this pair by eye if the mask looks wrong

objects.name: robed figure clipped by the left edge
objects.note: drawn in fine 白描 outline with no wash at all, which is why it disappears at thumbnail size -- torso with a sash, a pleated lower robe and one foot are legible; the head is cut off by the tile edge. Continues into t001. Robe and hem only

objects.name: pale bare silk at the bottom left edge
objects.note: a thin sliver of untouched silk beside the dark rocks with one or two faint horizontal strokes in it. UNCERTAIN: this is most likely the river surface or its far bank carrying over from t000/t001/t004, but at this tile's edge there is not enough of it to call water with confidence. Left as void rather than guessing ripple
